newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank eases liquidity shortage.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank eases liquidity shortage.

text.p: The Dutch central bank said on Friday it had provided 240 million guilders of overnight credit to the money market at the marginal advance facility rate of 4.5 percent just ahead of the cash reserve expiry today.

Dealers were suprised that a participant had been short of this amount of liquidity as last week's seven-day advances pact was ample and the central bank provided extra liquidity on Thursday with a guilder-dollar swap.
On Thursday the Dutch central bank offered a currency swap of almost 600 million guilders to ease the sudden liquidity shortage in the market.
A central bank spokesman said the unexpected shortage of liquidity had occured last weekend and that it had decided to relax the market with a currency-swap on Thursday.
He declined to give the reasons behind the unexpected liquidity shortage.

Another central bank spokesman said participants had preferred a currency swap to reduce the need for liquidity rather than offering an extra advances pact on top of the advances facility already running.
"Some participants in the money market preferred a currency swap," he said.
The central bank said the need for obtaining liquidity at the marginal advance facility would have been even greater if it had not relaxed the need for liquidity with the currency swap.

Call money rates rose above 3.00 percent bid just after the new cash reserve requirement took effect in early trade on Friday, but started slipping after the central bank allocated an ample amount under the new advances pact.
The central bank allocated 4.45 billion guilders to the money market under a seven-day special advances pact at an unchanged rate of 2.90 percent this morning.
Individual banks received 17.2 percent of the amount they had applied for, with the central bank setting a ceiling of 4.5 billion guilders on applications.
"This was more than expected," said one dealer, adding call money rates drooped to 2.75 percent bid from a bid price between 3.00 and 3.125 earlier.
Other rates were stable, with three-month deposits bid at an unchanged 3.12 percent.
The guilder was slightly weaker against the mark at 112.575 per 100 marks versus 112.565 on Thursday.
